meaning: Whatever it takes, however much it requires.
japanese: どんな代償を払ってでも。
cue: One outcome matters more than anything else. State it.
reply: We need to protect the data at any cost.
replyJapanese: どんな代償を払っても、データは守る必要があります。
transferReply: I avoid night shifts at any cost.
transferReplyJapanese: 夜勤だけは、何としても避けています。
nuance: Comes after the verb phrase. Stronger than at all costs in feeling, though they overlap.
nuanceJapanese: 動詞句のあとに置く。at all costs と重なるが、より強い響きになる。

meaning: Very near, so you can see the detail.
japanese: すぐ間近で、細部まで見える距離で。
cue: Describe seeing an animal on a walk.
reply: We saw a deer at close quarters for the first time.
replyJapanese: 初めて、鹿をすぐ間近で見ました。
transferReply: At close quarters you can see every join.
transferReplyJapanese: 間近で見ると、継ぎ目がすべて分かります。
nuance: Quarters is always plural. It implies close enough to observe, not merely nearby.
nuanceJapanese: quarters はつねに複数形。単に近いのではなく、観察できる距離を指す。

meaning: Working as hard as is possible.
japanese: 余力なく、目いっぱい動いている。
cue: A team cannot take on anything more. Explain.
reply: The department is at full stretch until April.
replyJapanese: 4月まで、その部署は手いっぱいです。
transferReply: The clinic runs at full stretch every winter.
transferReplyJapanese: あの診療所は、毎冬フル稼働です。
nuance: British. Stretch takes no article. It describes capacity, not effort or enthusiasm.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、stretch に冠詞は付かない。意欲ではなく、処理能力の限界を表す。

meaning: With no pattern or plan behind the choice.
japanese: 規則性なく、無作為に。
cue: Explain how samples were selected.
reply: We picked twenty files at random.
replyJapanese: 20件のファイルを、無作為に選びました。
transferReply: It plays the tracks at random.
transferReplyJapanese: 曲は順不同で再生されます。
nuance: Random takes no article. It claims no pattern, which matters when describing a method.
nuanceJapanese: random に冠詞は付かない。規則性がないことを示すので、方法の説明で重要になる。

meaning: With very little warning beforehand.
japanese: 直前になって、急に。
cue: Someone stepped in to help with almost no warning.
reply: She covered the class at short notice.
replyJapanese: 彼女は急な話で、授業を代わってくれました。
transferReply: Times can change at short notice, so please check.
transferReplyJapanese: 時間は直前に変わることがあるので、ご確認ください。
nuance: British; American English says on short notice. Notice takes no article.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では on short notice と言う。notice に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: In the most advanced or most prominent position.
japanese: 最前線にいて、先頭を走っている。
cue: Describe a group leading in its field.
reply: That lab is at the forefront of the research.
replyJapanese: あの研究室は、その分野の最前線にいます。
transferReply: Safety stays at the forefront of every decision.
transferReplyJapanese: どの判断でも、安全を最優先に置いています。
frame: Be at the forefront of something
nuance: Of introduces the field. It can mean leading a field or being uppermost in mind.
nuanceJapanese: 分野は of で示す。分野を先導する意味と、最も重視するという意味がある。

meaning: In charge of an organisation.
japanese: 組織の舵取りをする立場にある。
cue: A new leader has taken over. Report it.
reply: With her at the helm, things move faster.
replyJapanese: 彼女が舵を取るようになって、物事が速く進みます。
transferReply: He was at the helm for eighteen years.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は18年にわたって、組織を率いました。
frame: Be at the helm of something
nuance: From sailing. Helm takes the. It suits organisations rather than small teams.
nuanceJapanese: 帆走に由来し、helm には the を付ける。小さなチームより、組織について使う。

meaning: Support the side or option that turns out to lose.
japanese: 勝ち目のないほうに、肩入れしてしまう。
cue: A supplier you chose went out of business.
reply: We backed the wrong horse with that contract.
replyJapanese: あの契約では、選ぶ相手を誤りました。
transferReply: Plenty of people backed the wrong horse that year.
transferReplyJapanese: あの年は、見込み違いをした人が大勢いました。
nuance: From racing. It reports a wrong choice with hindsight, not a moral fault.
nuanceJapanese: 競馬に由来。道義的な非ではなく、結果的な選択ミスを述べる表現。

meaning: Value received for the money spent.
japanese: 払った金額に対して得られる価値。
cue: Compare two options of different price.
reply: The cheaper tool gives more bang for your buck.
replyJapanese: 安いほうの道具のほうが、費用対効果に優れます。
transferReply: There's real bang for your buck in the annual pass.
transferReplyJapanese: 年間パスは、実際に費用に見合う価値があります。
nuance: Informal and American in origin. Usually after more or better.
nuanceJapanese: もとはくだけたアメリカ英語。more や better のあとに置くことが多い。

meaning: Very soon, sooner than expected.
japanese: 気がつけば、あっという間に。
cue: A friend dreads a long wait. Reassure them.
reply: It'll be spring before you know it.
replyJapanese: 気がつけば、すぐ春になりますよ。
transferReply: Before you know it they're taller than you.
transferReplyJapanese: 気がつけば、自分より背が高くなっています。
nuance: Fixed with you even when talking about someone else. It can open or close a sentence.
nuanceJapanese: 他人の話でも you の形は変わらない。文頭にも文末にも置ける。

meaning: Driving a vehicle.
japanese: 運転席にいる。運転している。
cue: Discuss who will drive on a long trip.
reply: I'd rather not be behind the wheel after ten.
replyJapanese: 10時を過ぎたら、運転はしたくありません。
transferReply: She was behind the wheel for six hours.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は6時間、運転し続けました。
nuance: Wheel takes the. It refers to driving specifically, not to being in the car.
nuanceJapanese: wheel には the を付ける。同乗ではなく、運転していることを指す。

meaning: Suddenly lose your temper.
japanese: 堪忍袋の緒が切れる。
cue: Someone reacted furiously to a third repeated error.
reply: He blew a fuse when it happened again.
replyJapanese: また同じことが起きて、彼は堪忍袋の緒が切れました。
transferReply: Mention the deadline carefully or she'll blow a fuse.
transferReplyJapanese: 締め切りの話は慎重に。彼女が激怒しかねません。
nuance: Informal. Blow is irregular: blew, blown. It describes a sudden outburst, not lasting anger.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現。blow は不規則変化で blew、blown。続く怒りではなく、突発的な爆発を指す。

meaning: Publicly report wrongdoing inside an organisation.
japanese: 組織内の不正を、公に告発する。
cue: An employee reported a safety problem publicly.
reply: She blew the whistle on the testing shortcuts.
replyJapanese: 彼女は検査の手抜きについて、内部から告発しました。
transferReply: The law protects anyone who blows the whistle.
transferReplyJapanese: 法律は、内部告発する人を保護します。
nuance: On introduces the wrongdoing. The noun is a whistleblower, written as one word.
nuanceJapanese: 不正の内容は on で示す。名詞は whistleblower と1語で書く。

phrase: until you are blue in the face
meaning: For as long as you like, with no effect.
japanese: いくら言っても、無駄なまま。
cue: Repeated requests have changed nothing.
reply: You can ask until you are blue in the face.
replyJapanese: いくら頼んでも、無駄でしょう。
transferReply: We argued until we were blue in the face.
transferReplyJapanese: 議論し尽くしましたが、何も変わりませんでした。
frame: Until you are blue in the face
aliases: until we were blue in the face
nuance: Always follows a verb of speaking or asking. It stresses futility, not the length of time.
nuanceJapanese: 話す・頼むといった動詞のあとに置く。時間の長さより、無駄であることを強調する。

meaning: End a situation where neither side will move.
japanese: 膠着状態を、打開する。
cue: Two sides have refused to move for weeks.
reply: One small concession broke the deadlock.
replyJapanese: ひとつの小さな譲歩が、膠着状態を打開しました。
transferCue: Describe a goal in a tied match.
transferReply: A header broke the deadlock in the second half.
transferReplyJapanese: 後半のヘディングが、均衡を破りました。
nuance: Deadlock takes the. Break is irregular: broke, broken. Used in negotiation and in sport.
nuanceJapanese: deadlock には the を付ける。break は不規則変化で broke、broken。交渉にもスポーツにも使う。

meaning: A short period of relief before continuing.
japanese: 一息つくための、短い余裕。
cue: A deadline moved and gave the team relief.
reply: The extra week gives us some breathing space.
replyJapanese: 1週間延びて、少し余裕ができました。
transferReply: The payment holiday gave them breathing space.
transferReplyJapanese: 支払いの猶予で、彼らは一息つけました。
nuance: Uncountable, so no article, though some is common. It implies the pressure returns afterwards.
nuanceJapanese: 不可算なので冠詞は付かないが、some を添えることは多い。あとでまた圧力が戻る含みがある。

meaning: By an extremely small margin.
japanese: ごくわずかの差で。
cue: A result was decided by the narrowest margin.
reply: They won by a whisker.
replyJapanese: 彼らは、ごくわずかの差で勝ちました。
transferReply: I missed it by a whisker.
transferReplyJapanese: ほんのわずかの差で、乗り損ねました。
nuance: Follows a verb of winning, losing or missing. Whisker takes a and is always singular.
nuanceJapanese: 勝ち負けや取り逃しを表す動詞のあとに置く。whisker には a を付け、つねに単数。

meaning: Gradually, in small stages.
japanese: 少しずつ、段階を踏んで。
cue: A change happened slowly rather than at once.
reply: The style changed by degrees over ten years.
replyJapanese: その作風は、10年かけて少しずつ変わりました。
transferReply: She got stronger by degrees through the spring.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は春のあいだに、少しずつ回復していきました。
nuance: Degrees is always plural and takes no article. Slightly formal and literary.
nuanceJapanese: degrees はつねに複数形で、冠詞は付かない。やや改まった文語的な響き。

meaning: Officially stop an activity.
japanese: 正式に、activity を打ち切る。
cue: A trial is producing no useful result. Propose stopping.
reply: I'd call a halt to the trial now.
replyJapanese: この試験は、もう打ち切るべきでしょう。
transferCue: Describe stopping work in bad weather.
transferReply: They called a halt at four because of the wind.
transferReplyJapanese: 風のため、4時に作業が打ち切られました。
nuance: To introduces the activity. More formal and more final than stop.
nuanceJapanese: 対象は to で示す。stop より改まっていて、決定的な響きになる。

meaning: Spoil the mood of an otherwise good occasion.
japanese: よいはずの場に、影を落とす。
cue: Bad news arrived during a celebration.
reply: The news cast a shadow over the whole evening.
replyJapanese: あの知らせが、夜全体に影を落としました。
transferCue: Describe an event affected by a dispute.
transferReply: The disagreement cast a shadow over the reunion.
transferReplyJapanese: あの対立が、同窓会に影を落としました。
frame: Something casts a shadow over something
nuance: Cast is irregular and unchanged: cast. The cause is the subject.
nuanceJapanese: cast は不規則変化で、過去形も cast のまま。主語は原因のほう。

meaning: Pause to rest, or be briefly startled.
japanese: 息を整える。また、はっと息をのむ。
cue: You have climbed a steep hill.
reply: Give me a second to catch my breath.
replyJapanese: 少し息を整えさせてください。
transferReply: The view made me catch my breath.
transferReplyJapanese: あの眺めには、思わず息をのみました。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Two senses: recovering, and being momentarily startled.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。「息を整える」と「はっとする」の2つの意味がある。

meaning: Keep changing your plans or methods.
japanese: やり方をころころ変える。
cue: A project has changed direction four times.
reply: We can't keep chopping and changing like this.
replyJapanese: こう何度も方針を変えていては、進みません。
transferReply: They chopped and changed until the price went up.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らが迷っているうちに、値段が上がりました。
nuance: British and informal. The two verbs stay together in that order, usually in the continuous.
nuanceJapanese: くだけたイギリス英語。2つの動詞はこの順で一体として使い、ふつう進行形。

meaning: Obvious and leaving no room for doubt.
japanese: はっきりしていて、疑いの余地がない。
cue: A decision is not as simple as it looks.
reply: The case isn't as clear-cut as it seems.
replyJapanese: この件は、見た目ほど明快ではありません。
transferReply: The results were clear-cut for once.
transferReplyJapanese: 今回に限っては、結果は明快でした。
nuance: Always hyphenated. It describes evidence and decisions, not physical edges.
nuanceJapanese: つねにハイフンでつなぐ。物の輪郭ではなく、証拠や判断について使う。

meaning: A narrow escape from something bad.
japanese: あやうく難を逃れたこと。
cue: You nearly missed an important connection.
reply: That was a close shave — two minutes to spare.
replyJapanese: ぎりぎりでした。残りは2分です。
transferReply: The cyclist had a close shave at the junction.
transferReplyJapanese: あの自転車は、交差点であやうく事故になるところでした。
nuance: Countable, so a close shave. It reports relief rather than blame.
nuanceJapanese: 可算名詞なので a close shave となる。責任追及ではなく、安堵を伝える表現。

meaning: Receive criticism or attention, usually unwelcome.
japanese: 批判などを、まともに受ける。
cue: A decision attracted a lot of complaints.
reply: The new timetable came in for a lot of criticism.
replyJapanese: 新しい時刻表は、多くの批判を受けました。
transferReply: The cover came in for particular praise.
transferReplyJapanese: 表紙はとくに、高い評価を受けました。
nuance: Inseparable, usually with criticism, praise or attention. Come is irregular: came.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、criticism、praise、attention と組み合わせることが多い。come は不規則変化で came。

meaning: Start to have an effect on a situation.
japanese: 影響を及ぼし始める。
cue: A factor becomes relevant only at a certain point.
reply: Cost only comes into play above fifty units.
replyJapanese: 費用が効いてくるのは、50個を超えてからです。
transferReply: The wind came into play on the last lap.
transferReplyJapanese: 最終周で、風が影響し始めました。
nuance: Play takes no article. The factor is the subject, and it implies the effect starts at a point.
nuanceJapanese: play に冠詞は付かない。主語は要因のほうで、ある時点から効き始める含みがある。

meaning: Start fighting physically after an argument.
japanese: 口論の末に、殴り合いになる。
cue: An argument nearly became physical. Describe it.
reply: They almost came to blows over the parking.
replyJapanese: 駐車の件で、二人はあやうく殴り合いになりかけました。
transferCue: Describe a heated but controlled debate.
transferReply: It was fierce, but nobody came to blows.
transferReplyJapanese: 激しい議論でしたが、手が出ることはありませんでした。
nuance: Blows is always plural. Often with almost or nearly, since the fight usually does not happen.
nuanceJapanese: blows はつねに複数形。実際には至らないことが多く、almost や nearly を伴う。

meaning: Happen, especially as predicted.
japanese: 予言や予測どおりに、実際に起こる。
cue: A forecast from years ago turned out right.
reply: Everything she predicted came to pass.
replyJapanese: 彼女が予測したことは、すべて現実になりました。
transferCue: Describe a hope that was not realised.
transferReply: That plan never came to pass.
transferReplyJapanese: あの計画は、実現しませんでした。
nuance: Formal and slightly literary. Pass takes no article, and the event is the subject.
nuanceJapanese: 改まった、やや文語的な表現。pass に冠詞は付かず、主語は出来事のほう。

meaning: Realise afterwards how much harm something caused.
japanese: あとになって、その代償の大きさを思い知る。
cue: A quick decision caused long-term damage.
reply: We're counting the cost of that shortcut now.
replyJapanese: あの近道の代償を、今になって思い知っています。
transferCue: Describe a community after a storm.
transferReply: The village is still counting the cost.
transferReplyJapanese: その村は、いまだに被害の大きさに直面しています。
nuance: Cost takes the and is singular. It looks back at damage, not forward at a price.
nuanceJapanese: cost には the を付け、単数。将来の値段ではなく、すでに生じた損害を振り返る表現。

meaning: Already decided and not open to discussion.
japanese: すでに決まっていて、議論の余地がない。
cue: A colleague asks whether input is still wanted.
reply: It isn't cut and dried yet, so do comment.
replyJapanese: まだ決定ではないので、ぜひ意見をください。
transferReply: The rule is cut and dried on this point.
transferReplyJapanese: この点について、規則は明快です。
nuance: Fixed word order. Often in the negative, to show a decision is still open.
nuanceJapanese: 語順は固定。まだ決まっていないことを示すため、否定形で使うことが多い。

meaning: A course of action that leads nowhere.
japanese: 行き止まりで、先のない道。
cue: A line of investigation produced nothing.
reply: That line of enquiry was a dead end.
replyJapanese: あの方向の調査は、行き止まりでした。
transferCue: Describe a job with no prospects.
transferReply: He left because it felt like a dead end.
transferReplyJapanese: 先がないと感じて、彼は辞めました。
nuance: Countable and also literal for streets. Dead-end before a noun, as in a dead-end job.
nuanceJapanese: 可算名詞で、道の行き止まりの意味もある。名詞の前では dead-end job のようにハイフンでつなぐ。

meaning: Find extra effort or money when it is hard to.
japanese: 苦しいなかで、力や資金を絞り出す。
cue: A team recovered in the last part of a contest.
reply: They dug deep in the final twenty minutes.
replyJapanese: 最後の20分、彼らは力を振り絞りました。
transferReply: People dug deep and the target was met.
transferReplyJapanese: みんなが寄付を惜しまず、目標に届きました。
nuance: Intransitive. Dig is irregular: dug. Used for effort and for money alike.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。dig は不規則変化で dug。努力にも金銭にも使う。

meaning: Circulate among many people.
japanese: 人づてに、あちこちに出回る。
cue: A rumour has reached everyone in an office.
reply: That story has been doing the rounds all week.
replyJapanese: その話は、今週ずっと出回っています。
transferReply: She did the rounds and spoke to every team.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は各所を回って、全チームと話しました。
nuance: Rounds is always plural. American English says make the rounds.
nuanceJapanese: rounds はつねに複数形。アメリカ英語では make the rounds と言う。

meaning: Point out a similarity between two things.
japanese: 二つのあいだに、共通点を見いだす。
cue: Two situations resemble each other. Point it out.
reply: You can draw a parallel with the 2019 shortage.
replyJapanese: 2019年の品不足と、重ねて見ることができます。
transferReply: She draws a parallel between the two decades.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は、その2つの年代を重ね合わせて論じています。
frame: Draw a parallel between two things
nuance: Between introduces two things, with introduces one. Draw is irregular: drew, drawn.
nuanceJapanese: 二者なら between、一方だけなら with を使う。draw は不規則変化で drew、drawn。

meaning: Suggest something indirectly.
japanese: それとなく、ほのめかす。
cue: You want someone to guess what you would like.
reply: I dropped a hint about the concert tickets.
replyJapanese: コンサートのチケットのことを、それとなくほのめかしました。
transferCue: Describe an indirect request at work.
transferReply: She dropped a hint that the date might move.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は日程が動くかもしれないと、ほのめかしました。
nuance: Countable: drop a hint, drop hints. About introduces the topic, that introduces the content.
nuanceJapanese: 可算で、drop a hint、drop hints と言う。話題は about、内容は that で示す。

meaning: Do enough work to justify what you are given.
japanese: 受け取る分に見合う働きをする。
cue: Describe a useful piece of equipment.
reply: That old van has earned its keep many times over.
replyJapanese: あの古いバンは、元を何倍も取っています。
transferCue: Describe a family member helping out.
transferReply: He earns his keep by doing all the cooking.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は料理を全部引き受けて、分をわきまえています。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Used for people and for equipment alike.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。人にも道具にも使う。

meaning: Accept the truth of a situation.
japanese: 現実を、そのまま受け入れる。
cue: A plan is clearly not going to work.
reply: Let's face facts — it won't be ready.
replyJapanese: 現実を見ましょう。間に合いません。
transferReply: I had to face facts about my knee.
transferReplyJapanese: 膝のことは、現実を受け入れるしかありませんでした。
nuance: Facts takes no article in this phrase. Let's face facts often opens an unwelcome conclusion.
nuanceJapanese: この表現では facts に冠詞を付けない。let's face facts は、歓迎されない結論の前置きによく使う。

meaning: Be abandoned before being finished.
japanese: 途中で見捨てられ、立ち消えになる。
cue: Several good ideas were never pursued.
reply: Two of the proposals fell by the wayside.
replyJapanese: 提案のうち2件は、途中で立ち消えになりました。
transferReply: My running fell by the wayside in November.
transferReplyJapanese: ランニングは、11月に立ち消えになりました。
nuance: Fall is irregular: fell, fallen. The abandoned thing is the subject.
nuanceJapanese: fall は不規則変化で fell、fallen。主語は立ち消えになったもの。

meaning: Start following the rules or the agreed approach.
japanese: 方針に従って、足並みをそろえる。
cue: A department resisted a change and then accepted it.
reply: They fell into line once the policy was published.
replyJapanese: 方針が公表されると、彼らも足並みをそろえました。
transferCue: Describe a group accepting a decision.
transferReply: Everyone fell into line after the vote.
transferReplyJapanese: 採決のあと、全員が方針に従いました。
nuance: Line takes no article. It implies earlier resistance that has now ended.
nuanceJapanese: line に冠詞は付かない。それまで抵抗があったことを含意する。

meaning: Feel comfortable and relaxed somewhere.
japanese: くつろいで、居心地よく感じる。
cue: Welcome a guest to your house.
reply: Please feel at home — the kettle's there.
replyJapanese: どうぞくつろいでください。やかんはそこにあります。
transferCue: Describe settling into a new team.
transferReply: It took a month before I felt at home there.
transferReplyJapanese: あそこに馴染むまで、1か月かかりました。
nuance: Home takes no article. Feel is irregular: felt. It describes comfort, not ownership.
nuanceJapanese: home に冠詞は付かない。feel は不規則変化で felt。所有ではなく、居心地の話。

meaning: Avoid doing something because you are reluctant.
japanese: 気が進まず、避けて通る。
cue: An organisation avoids a difficult subject.
reply: They fight shy of publishing the raw numbers.
replyJapanese: 彼らは生の数字を公表することを、避けています。
transferReply: I've fought shy of that conversation for weeks.
transferReplyJapanese: あの話し合いを、何週間も避けてきました。
nuance: Inseparable and slightly formal. Fight is irregular: fought. Of is followed by a noun or -ing.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない、やや改まった表現。fight は不規則変化で fought。of のあとは名詞か -ing。

meaning: Deal with the most important matter before anything else.
japanese: まずは、いちばん大事なことから。
cue: A meeting is drifting into detail too early.
reply: First things first — do we have the budget?
replyJapanese: まず大事なことから。予算はあるのでしょうか。
transferReply: First things first, I need coffee.
transferReplyJapanese: まずは何より、コーヒーが必要です。
nuance: Fixed and always plural. It opens a sentence and reorders priorities.
nuanceJapanese: 形が固定し、つねに複数形。文頭に置いて、優先順位を整理する。

meaning: Directly contradict what is expected or accepted.
japanese: 通念や予想に、真っ向から逆らう。
cue: A finding contradicts established thinking.
reply: The result flies in the face of everything we assumed.
replyJapanese: その結果は、こちらの前提すべてに反しています。
transferReply: The plan flies in the face of the survey.
transferReplyJapanese: その計画は、調査結果に真っ向から反しています。
frame: Something flies in the face of something
nuance: Fly is irregular: flew, flown. The contradicting thing is the subject.
nuanceJapanese: fly は不規則変化で flew、flown。主語は矛盾しているほう。

meaning: Do the same work or make the same choices as someone before you.
japanese: 先人と同じ道を、あとから歩む。
cue: A child has entered the same profession as a parent.
reply: She followed in her mother's footsteps into teaching.
replyJapanese: 彼女は母親と同じく、教える道に進みました。
transferReply: He's following in his predecessor's footsteps carefully.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は前任者の道筋を、慎重にたどっています。
nuance: The possessive names the person followed and footsteps is always plural.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は先を歩いた人を示し、footsteps はつねに複数形。

meaning: Used to introduce the first of several reasons.
japanese: まず第一に、という切り出し方。
cue: You have several objections to a plan.
reply: For a start, nobody has checked the cost.
replyJapanese: まず第一に、費用を誰も確認していません。
transferCue: Give the first of several reasons.
transferReply: It's too small, for a start.
transferReplyJapanese: まず第一に、狭すぎます。
nuance: British; American English says for starters. It signals that more reasons follow.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では for starters と言う。理由がまだ続くことを示す。

meaning: Because you are worried that something bad might happen.
japanese: そうなることを恐れて。
cue: Someone stayed silent to avoid causing trouble.
reply: She said nothing for fear of making it worse.
replyJapanese: 事態を悪化させることを恐れて、彼女は黙っていました。
transferReply: We left early for fear of missing the last train.
transferReplyJapanese: 終電を逃すことを恐れて、早めに出ました。
nuance: Followed by a noun or -ing, never by to. Fear takes no article.
nuanceJapanese: 名詞か -ing を続け、to は続かない。fear に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: Used to add a related point that is equally true.
japanese: ついでに言えば、それについても同じだ。
cue: An objection applies to more than one option.
reply: That's true of the second option, and the third for that matter.
replyJapanese: それは2つ目にも、ついでに言えば3つ目にも当てはまります。
transferReply: I've never been there. Nor to Spain, for that matter.
transferReplyJapanese: 行ったことがありません。ついでに言えば、スペインにも。
nuance: Usually at the end of a clause after a comma. It extends what you just said to another case.
nuanceJapanese: 節の末尾にコンマを添えて置くのがふつう。直前の内容を別の場合にも広げる。

meaning: Start doing something quickly.
japanese: さっそく取りかかる。
cue: A deadline is close and nothing has started.
reply: We'd better get cracking if it's due at five.
replyJapanese: 5時締め切りなら、さっそく取りかかりましょう。
transferCue: Encourage a group after a break.
transferReply: Right, let's get cracking on the second half.
transferReplyJapanese: さて、後半にさっそく取りかかりましょう。
nuance: Intransitive and informal; on introduces the task. Always about starting, not continuing.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞のくだけた表現で、作業は on で示す。継続ではなく、着手についての語。

phrase: get into the swing of things
meaning: Become comfortable with a new routine.
japanese: 新しい流れに、慣れて乗ってくる。
cue: A new colleague is settling in.
reply: Give it a fortnight and you'll get into the swing of things.
replyJapanese: 2週間もすれば、流れに慣れてきますよ。
transferReply: It took a week to get into the swing of things again.
transferReplyJapanese: また調子を取り戻すのに、1週間かかりました。
frame: Get into the swing of things
aliases: get into the swing of it
nuance: Swing takes the. Of things or of it both work, and the phrase implies a gradual adjustment.
nuanceJapanese: swing には the を付ける。of things も of it も使え、徐々に慣れることを含意する。

meaning: Understand what someone is indirectly telling you.
japanese: 言わんとすることを、察する。
cue: Someone kept looking at the clock. Interpret it.
reply: He kept checking his watch, so I got the message.
replyJapanese: 彼が時計ばかり見ていたので、察しました。
transferReply: I said it twice and they still didn't get the message.
transferReplyJapanese: 2回言いましたが、まだ伝わっていませんでした。
nuance: Message takes the. It implies the point was made indirectly rather than stated.
nuanceJapanese: message には the を付ける。直接言わず、ほのめかされたことを含意する。

meaning: Work out where you are or how things work.
japanese: 自分の位置や状況を、つかむ。
cue: A new colleague needs time to orient themselves.
reply: Take a week to get your bearings before you decide.
replyJapanese: 決める前に、1週間かけて状況をつかんでください。
transferCue: Describe arriving in an unfamiliar city.
transferReply: I walked around to get my bearings.
transferReplyJapanese: 位置関係をつかむために、歩いて回りました。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and bearings is always plural. Literal and figurative.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせ、bearings はつねに複数形。文字どおりにも比喩的にも使う。

meaning: Deliberately keep well away from someone or something.
japanese: あえて、大きく距離を取る。
cue: A topic always causes trouble. Advise avoiding it.
reply: I'd give that subject a wide berth today.
replyJapanese: 今日は、その話題には近づかないほうがいいでしょう。
transferReply: We gave the main road a wide berth.
transferReplyJapanese: 大通りは、大きく避けて通りました。
nuance: From sailing. The thing avoided goes between give and a. Berth is always singular here.
nuanceJapanese: 帆走に由来。避ける対象は give と a のあいだに置く。ここでの berth は単数。

meaning: Formally tell an employer or landlord you are leaving.
japanese: 退職や退去を、正式に申し出る。
cue: Someone has decided to leave their job.
reply: She gave notice on Monday morning.
replyJapanese: 彼女は月曜の朝、退職を申し出ました。
transferReply: We have to give notice two months in advance.
transferReplyJapanese: 退去は、2か月前に申し出る必要があります。
nuance: Notice takes no article. It refers to the formal period, not to informing someone generally.
nuanceJapanese: notice に冠詞は付かない。一般的な通知ではなく、正式な予告期間を指す。

meaning: Suddenly start talking about something unrelated.
japanese: 話が急にそれて、別の方向へ行く。
cue: A discussion left the topic entirely.
reply: We went off at a tangent about parking.
replyJapanese: 駐車の話に、すっかり脱線しました。
transferCue: Bring a meeting back on topic.
transferReply: Sorry, I went off at a tangent there.
transferReplyJapanese: すみません、話がそれました。
nuance: British uses at, American on. Tangent takes a and is singular.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語では at、アメリカ英語では on。tangent には a を付け、単数。

meaning: Do something without real effort or interest.
japanese: 形だけこなして、気持ちが入っていない。
cue: A team is completing tasks without engagement.
reply: We're going through the motions rather than fixing it.
replyJapanese: 解決するのではなく、形だけこなしている状態です。
transferReply: The second half was just going through the motions.
transferReplyJapanese: 後半は、ただ形をなぞっているだけでした。
nuance: Motions is always plural with the. Always critical of the lack of genuine effort.
nuanceJapanese: motions は the を伴う複数形。本気でないことへの批判をつねに含む。

meaning: Do something with great enthusiasm and no restraint.
japanese: 思いきり、手をかけてやる。
cue: Someone decorated far beyond expectation.
reply: They really went to town on the decorations.
replyJapanese: 飾りつけに、思いきり手をかけていました。
transferReply: She went to town on the appendix.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は付録に、とことんこだわりました。
nuance: On introduces what was done lavishly. Town takes no article, and it is usually admiring.
nuanceJapanese: 対象は on で示す。town に冠詞は付かず、ふつうは感心した響きになる。

meaning: Accept something unpleasant without complaining.
japanese: 不満を言わずに、じっと我慢する。
cue: An uncomfortable situation cannot be changed.
reply: There's nothing to be done, so we grin and bear it.
replyJapanese: どうにもならないので、我慢するしかありません。
transferReply: Four hours in that seat — you just grin and bear it.
transferReplyJapanese: あの席で4時間。ただ耐えるしかありません。
nuance: Fixed with it. Bear is irregular: bore, borne. It accepts rather than solves.
nuanceJapanese: it を伴う固定表現。bear は不規則変化で bore、borne。解決ではなく受容を表す。

meaning: Easily and without any doubt.
japanese: 文句なしに。楽々と。
cue: One option is clearly the best.
reply: That's the best of the three, hands down.
replyJapanese: 3つのなかでは、文句なしにあれが最良です。
transferReply: They won hands down.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らは楽々と勝ちました。
nuance: Comes after the verb or at the end of the sentence. Hands is always plural.
nuanceJapanese: 動詞のあとか文末に置く。hands はつねに複数形。

meaning: Difficult and tiring to get through.
japanese: 骨が折れて、なかなか進まない。
cue: A book is worthwhile but demanding.
reply: The first hundred pages are hard going.
replyJapanese: 最初の100ページは、読み進めるのが骨です。
transferReply: The last stretch was hard going in the heat.
transferReplyJapanese: 最後の区間は、暑さもあって骨が折れました。
nuance: British and uncountable, so no article. Used about books, journeys and conversations.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語の不可算表現で、冠詞は付かない。本や道のり、会話について使う。

meaning: Have a strong like or dislike for something.
japanese: やたらと好き、あるいは苦手である。
cue: A colleague always chooses the same colour.
reply: She has a thing about green.
replyJapanese: 彼女は緑にこだわりがあります。
transferReply: I have a thing about lifts, so I'll take the stairs.
transferReplyJapanese: エレベーターが苦手なので、階段にします。
nuance: Informal, and the feeling can be positive or negative. Context makes it clear which.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、好意にも嫌悪にもなる。どちらかは文脈で分かる。

meaning: Have an ability that others did not expect.
japanese: そんな力があるとは思われていなかった。
cue: Someone performed far better than expected.
reply: I didn't know you had it in you.
replyJapanese: そんな力があるとは知りませんでした。
transferReply: You have it in you — just start.
transferReplyJapanese: あなたならできます。まず始めましょう。
nuance: Fixed with it; the pronoun follows the person. Usually admiring surprise.
nuanceJapanese: it を伴う固定表現で、代名詞は本人に合わせる。ふつうは感心した驚きを表す。

meaning: Sometimes good and sometimes not, with no consistency.
japanese: 当たり外れがあって、安定しない。
cue: A restaurant is inconsistent. Describe it.
reply: The food there is hit and miss.
replyJapanese: あの店の料理は、当たり外れがあります。
transferReply: The scanner is hit and miss with old paper.
transferReplyJapanese: あの読み取り機は、古い紙だと当たり外れがあります。
nuance: Both and and or are used. Fixed order, and it describes inconsistency rather than poor quality.
nuanceJapanese: and と or のどちらも使う。語順は固定で、質の低さではなく不安定さを表す。

meaning: Become widely reported news.
japanese: 大きく報道されて、話題になる。
cue: A local story became national news.
reply: The closure hit the headlines within a day.
replyJapanese: その閉鎖は、1日で大きく報じられました。
transferReply: They settled quietly rather than hit the headlines.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らは大きく報じられるより、静かに和解しました。
nuance: Headlines is always plural with the. Hit is irregular and unchanged: hit.
nuanceJapanese: headlines は the を伴う複数形。hit は不規則変化で、形は変わらない。

meaning: Have the main influence over something.
japanese: 大きな影響力を持って、支配している。
cue: One view dominates a field. Describe it.
reply: That theory held sway for thirty years.
replyJapanese: その説は、30年にわたって主流でした。
transferCue: Describe who decides in a group.
transferReply: Cost still holds sway over every decision.
transferReplyJapanese: どの判断でも、いまだに費用が支配的です。
nuance: Sway takes no article. Formal, and it describes dominance over time rather than a single decision.
nuanceJapanese: sway に冠詞は付かない。改まった表現で、一度の決定より長期の支配を表す。

meaning: Angry and flustered.
japanese: かっとなって、いきり立っている。
cue: Someone became agitated during a discussion.
reply: He got hot under the collar about the wording.
replyJapanese: 彼は表現のことで、いきり立っていました。
transferReply: There's no need to get hot under the collar.
transferReplyJapanese: そう、いきり立つ必要はありません。
nuance: Usually with get. Collar takes the. It suggests visible agitation rather than deep anger.
nuanceJapanese: ふつう get と使い、collar には the を付ける。深い怒りより、表に出た動揺を表す。

meaning: Uncomfortable and not relaxed.
japanese: 落ち着かず、居心地が悪い。
cue: A guest seemed uncomfortable at a formal dinner.
reply: He looked ill at ease in the suit.
replyJapanese: スーツ姿の彼は、落ち着かない様子でした。
transferReply: I felt ill at ease for the first hour.
transferReplyJapanese: 最初の1時間は、落ち着きませんでした。
nuance: Fixed word order. Slightly formal; the opposite is at ease.
nuanceJapanese: 語順は固定。やや改まった表現で、反対は at ease。

meaning: Used before a very short summary.
japanese: ひとことで言えば。
cue: Someone asks for your overall verdict.
reply: In a word, disappointing.
replyJapanese: ひとことで言えば、残念でした。
transferReply: In a word, exhausting.
transferReplyJapanese: ひとことで言えば、へとへとです。
nuance: Opens the sentence and is usually followed by a single word or a short phrase.
nuanceJapanese: 文頭に置き、ふつうは一語か短い句を続ける。

meaning: Used before saying what you really think.
japanese: 正直に言うと。
cue: You are giving a candid opinion about a draft.
reply: In all honesty, the opening doesn't work.
replyJapanese: 正直に言うと、冒頭がうまくいっていません。
transferReply: In all honesty, I've never used one.
transferReplyJapanese: 正直なところ、使ったことがありません。
nuance: Opens the sentence, followed by a comma. It signals candour and softens what follows.
nuanceJapanese: 文頭に置いてコンマを続ける。率直さを示し、続く内容をやわらげる。

meaning: Seriously and properly, not as a trial.
japanese: 本格的に。本腰を入れて。
cue: Preparation has moved past the planning stage.
reply: Work begins in earnest on Monday.
replyJapanese: 月曜から、本格的に作業が始まります。
transferReply: He asked in earnest, not as a joke.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は冗談ではなく、本気で頼んできました。
nuance: Earnest takes no article. It contrasts with preliminary work or with joking.
nuanceJapanese: earnest に冠詞は付かない。準備段階や冗談との対比で使う。

meaning: Officially operating, or present in large numbers.
japanese: 効力を持って、実施されている。また、大挙して。
cue: Explain when a rule starts to apply.
reply: The new rules are in force from April.
replyJapanese: 新しい規則は、4月から効力を持ちます。
transferReply: Supporters turned out in force.
transferReplyJapanese: 支持者が、大挙して詰めかけました。
nuance: Force takes no article. Two senses that context separates easily: legally operating, and in large numbers.
nuanceJapanese: force に冠詞は付かない。「施行中」と「大挙して」の2つの意味は、文脈で容易に区別できる。

meaning: Being looked after by someone competent.
japanese: 信頼できる人に、任せられている。
cue: Reassure someone about a handover.
reply: You're in good hands with Naomi.
replyJapanese: ナオミさんに任せておけば安心です。
transferReply: He's in good hands at the kennel.
transferReplyJapanese: あの子はペットホテルで、よく見てもらっています。
nuance: Hands is always plural. With introduces the person trusted.
nuanceJapanese: hands はつねに複数形。任せる相手は with で示す。

meaning: As a joke rather than seriously.
japanese: 冗談として。本気ではなく。
cue: A remark was taken more seriously than intended.
reply: It was said in jest, but it landed badly.
replyJapanese: 冗談のつもりでしたが、受け取られ方がよくありませんでした。
transferReply: I only suggested it in jest.
transferReplyJapanese: 冗談で言っただけです。
nuance: Formal and slightly literary. Jest takes no article; in fun is the everyday alternative.
nuanceJapanese: 改まった、やや文語的な表現。jest に冠詞は付かない。日常では in fun を使う。

meaning: All at once, in a single action.
japanese: 一挙に、一回の動きで。
cue: One decision solved several problems together.
reply: The change fixed three issues in one fell swoop.
replyJapanese: その変更で、3つの問題が一挙に解決しました。
transferReply: She cleared the whole inbox in one fell swoop.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は受信箱を、一気に片づけました。
nuance: Fixed and slightly literary. Fell here is an old adjective, not the verb.
nuanceJapanese: 形が固定した、やや文語的な表現。ここでの fell は動詞ではなく古い形容詞。

meaning: Safe and undamaged after something risky.
japanese: 無事に、壊れずに。
cue: A fragile parcel survived the post.
reply: The glass arrived in one piece, thankfully.
replyJapanese: ありがたいことに、ガラスは無事に届きました。
transferCue: Describe returning from a difficult trip.
transferReply: We got back in one piece, which was the main thing.
transferReplyJapanese: 無事に戻れたので、それが何よりです。
nuance: Fixed. Used for objects and, lightly, for people after something demanding.
nuanceJapanese: 形は固定。物のほか、大変な経験のあとの人について軽く使う。

meaning: Easily visible, though people fail to notice.
japanese: 目の前にあるのに、気づかれない。
cue: A lost item was on the table all along.
reply: It was in plain sight the whole time.
replyJapanese: ずっと目の前にありました。
transferReply: The answer was hiding in plain sight.
transferReplyJapanese: 答えは、目の前に隠れていました。
nuance: Fixed. Often paired with hiding, which gives the sense of being overlooked despite visibility.
nuanceJapanese: 形は固定。hiding と組み合わせて、見えているのに見落とされる感じを出すことが多い。

meaning: In exactly those terms, explicitly.
japanese: はっきりそう言った、という形で。
cue: Someone implied something without stating it.
reply: He didn't say no in so many words.
replyJapanese: 彼は、はっきり断ったわけではありません。
transferReply: She told me, though not in so many words.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は伝えてきましたが、はっきり言葉にしたわけではありません。
nuance: Almost always in the negative. It marks the difference between implying and stating.
nuanceJapanese: ほぼつねに否定形。ほのめかしと明言の違いを示す。

meaning: Waiting to happen to someone in the future.
japanese: この先、その人を待ち受けている。
cue: Something is planned that a colleague does not know about.
reply: There's a surprise in store for her on Friday.
replyJapanese: 金曜に、彼女には驚きが待っています。
transferReply: Nobody knows what's in store for the industry.
transferReplyJapanese: この業界に何が待ち受けているか、誰にも分かりません。
nuance: Store takes no article. For introduces the person, and the subject is what awaits them.
nuanceJapanese: store に冠詞は付かない。対象の人は for で示し、主語は待ち受けているもの。

meaning: If a particular thing happens.
japanese: 万一そうなった場合には。
cue: Explain a contingency in a formal notice.
reply: In the event of cancellation, we refund in full.
replyJapanese: 万一中止となった場合、全額を返金します。
transferReply: In the event of fire, use the rear stairs.
transferReplyJapanese: 火災の際は、裏の階段をご利用ください。
nuance: Formal, followed by a noun. In the event that takes a clause instead.
nuanceJapanese: 改まった表現で、名詞を続ける。節を続けるときは in the event that を使う。

meaning: In the position most likely to be criticised or blamed.
japanese: いちばん批判を受けやすい立場にある。
cue: One department faces most of the scrutiny.
reply: Support is in the firing line this quarter.
replyJapanese: 今四半期は、サポート部門が矢面に立っています。
transferReply: Whoever speaks will be in the firing line.
transferReplyJapanese: 話す人は誰であれ、矢面に立つことになります。
nuance: British; American English says in the line of fire. About criticism, not literal danger.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では in the line of fire と言う。実際の危険ではなく、批判についての表現。

meaning: Considering a period far into the future.
japanese: 長い目で見れば。
cue: A costly choice will save money eventually.
reply: It's cheaper in the long term.
replyJapanese: 長い目で見れば、そのほうが安く済みます。
transferReply: It works now, but not in the long term.
transferReplyJapanese: 今は機能しますが、長い目で見れば無理があります。
nuance: Term takes the. Long-term with a hyphen goes before a noun, as in a long-term plan.
nuanceJapanese: term には the を付ける。名詞の前では a long-term plan のようにハイフンでつなぐ。

meaning: Publicly known rather than hidden.
japanese: 隠されず、公になっている。
cue: A difficult subject has finally been discussed.
reply: It's better to have it out in the open.
replyJapanese: 隠さず表に出したほうが、結局はよいです。
transferReply: Disagreements are kept in the open here.
transferReplyJapanese: ここでは、意見の対立も隠さず表に出します。
nuance: Often with out. Open takes the. It contrasts with keeping something hidden.
nuanceJapanese: out を伴うことが多く、open には the を付ける。隠すこととの対比で使う。

meaning: Ready and waiting for the right moment to appear.
japanese: 出番を待って、控えている。
cue: A replacement is already prepared.
reply: There's a successor waiting in the wings.
replyJapanese: 後任がすでに、出番を待って控えています。
transferReply: We keep a second option in the wings.
transferReplyJapanese: 第二の選択肢を、控えとして用意しています。
nuance: From the theatre. Wings is always plural with the, and it implies readiness rather than delay.
nuanceJapanese: 劇場に由来。wings は the を伴う複数形で、遅れではなく準備が整っていることを含意する。

meaning: Fortunate, given how things turned out.
japanese: 結果的に、かえってよかった。
cue: A cancelled plan turned out to be lucky.
reply: It's just as well we didn't book the earlier train.
replyJapanese: 早い電車を取らなくて、かえってよかったです。
transferReply: Just as well I brought a coat.
transferReplyJapanese: 上着を持ってきて、かえってよかったです。
nuance: Often with it's and a that clause, which can be dropped. It reports lucky timing after the fact.
nuanceJapanese: it's と that 節を伴うことが多く、that は省ける。結果的な幸運を、あとから述べる表現。

meaning: Control something so it does not grow too much.
japanese: 大きくなりすぎないよう、抑えておく。
cue: Costs must not rise further. State the aim.
reply: We need to keep travel costs in check.
replyJapanese: 出張費を、抑えておく必要があります。
transferReply: She kept her irritation in check throughout.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は終始、いらだちを抑えていました。
nuance: The object goes between keep and in. Check takes no article.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語は keep と in のあいだに置く。check に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: Watch how something develops.
japanese: 動きを、継続して把握しておく。
cue: A figure needs monitoring over the quarter.
reply: I keep tabs on the weekly numbers.
replyJapanese: 週次の数字は、私が継続して見ています。
transferReply: They keep tabs on what we publish.
transferReplyJapanese: 先方は、こちらの公表物を継続して見ています。
nuance: Tabs is always plural. Neutral about things, but slightly intrusive about people.
nuanceJapanese: tabs はつねに複数形。物については中立だが、人について使うと監視の含みが出る。

meaning: Avoid getting into trouble.
japanese: 問題を起こさず、身ぎれいにしている。
cue: Advise someone during a probation period.
reply: Keep your nose clean for the first six months.
replyJapanese: 最初の半年は、問題を起こさないようにしてください。
transferCue: Describe someone with a clean record.
transferReply: He kept his nose clean for twenty years.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は20年間、何の問題も起こしませんでした。
nuance: Informal; the possessive follows the subject. It implies temptation or risk nearby.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、所有格は主語に合わせる。周囲に誘惑や危険があることを含意する。

meaning: Be completely aware of something, despite acting otherwise.
japanese: 承知のうえで、そうしている。
cue: Someone asked a question they already knew the answer to.
reply: You know full well why it was refused.
replyJapanese: 断られた理由は、承知のはずです。
transferReply: I knew full well it would take longer.
transferReplyJapanese: もっと時間がかかることは、承知していました。
nuance: Know is irregular: knew, known. It usually carries a note of reproach when used about someone else.
nuanceJapanese: know は不規則変化で knew、known。他人について使うと、とがめる響きを帯びることが多い。

meaning: Have real expertise in your subject.
japanese: その分野を、しっかり心得ている。
cue: A specialist answered every question confidently.
reply: She really knows her stuff on tax.
replyJapanese: 税務について、彼女は本当によく心得ています。
transferReply: Use him — he knows his stuff.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼に頼んでください。よく分かっている人です。
nuance: Informal; the possessive follows the subject. Complimentary and about practical expertise.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、所有格は主語に合わせる。実務的な専門性をほめる言い方。

meaning: State rules firmly, in a way that allows no argument.
japanese: 有無を言わせず、規則を申し渡す。
cue: A manager set out strict expectations.
reply: He laid down the law about deadlines.
replyJapanese: 彼は締め切りについて、有無を言わせず申し渡しました。
transferReply: My grandmother laid down the law about mealtimes.
transferReplyJapanese: 祖母は食事の時間について、厳しく決めていました。
frame: Lay down the law about something
nuance: Lay is irregular: laid. Usually mildly critical of the manner, not the rule itself.
nuanceJapanese: lay は不規則変化で laid。規則そのものより、その伝え方への軽い批判を含むことが多い。

meaning: Reveal something accidentally.
japanese: うっかり、口を滑らせる。
cue: Someone revealed a surprise by mistake.
reply: He let slip that the party was on Saturday.
replyJapanese: 彼はうっかり、パーティーが土曜だと漏らしました。
transferReply: I let slip the price and regretted it.
transferReplyJapanese: うっかり値段を漏らして、後悔しました。
nuance: Let is irregular and unchanged: let. Usually followed by that and a clause.
nuanceJapanese: let は不規則変化で、形は変わらない。ふつう that 節を続ける。

meaning: Stay out of sight until attention passes.
japanese: ほとぼりが冷めるまで、目立たずにいる。
cue: Someone is avoiding attention after a controversy.
reply: He's lying low until the story fades.
replyJapanese: 彼は騒ぎが収まるまで、目立たないようにしています。
transferCue: Describe a quiet period at work.
transferReply: I lay low for a week after the review.
transferReplyJapanese: 評価のあと、1週間は目立たないようにしていました。
nuance: Lie is irregular: lay, lain. Not to be confused with lay, which takes an object.
nuanceJapanese: lie は不規則変化で lay、lain。目的語を取る lay と混同しない。

meaning: Forget what really matters while dealing with detail.
japanese: 細部に追われて、本来の目的を見失う。
cue: A project has become about process rather than purpose.
reply: We've lost sight of why we started this.
replyJapanese: なぜ始めたのかを、見失ってしまっています。
transferCue: Describe keeping a goal in mind.
transferReply: Don't lose sight of the reader.
transferReplyJapanese: 読み手のことを、見失わないでください。
nuance: Lose is irregular: lost. Sight takes no article, and the object is usually a purpose or a person.
nuanceJapanese: lose は不規則変化で lost。sight に冠詞は付かず、目的語は目的や人であることが多い。

meaning: Judge someone less strictly because of their situation.
japanese: 事情をくんで、厳しく見ないでおく。
cue: A colleague is underperforming while unwell.
reply: We should make allowances while she's recovering.
replyJapanese: 回復中のあいだは、事情をくむべきでしょう。
transferReply: Make allowances — it's his first week.
transferReplyJapanese: 大目に見てください。まだ初週です。
nuance: Allowances is always plural. For introduces the person or the circumstance.
nuanceJapanese: allowances はつねに複数形。対象の人や事情は for で示す。

meaning: Not apply a rule in one particular case.
japanese: 一度だけ、規則を適用しない。
cue: A customer asks for something outside policy.
reply: We can make an exception this once.
replyJapanese: 今回だけは、例外として対応できます。
transferReply: If we make an exception, everyone will ask.
transferReplyJapanese: 例外を作れば、みんなが求めてきます。
nuance: Countable: make an exception, make exceptions. For introduces who benefits.
nuanceJapanese: 可算で、make an exception、make exceptions と言う。対象は for で示す。

meaning: Prevent an argument from breaking out.
japanese: 波風が立たないように収める。
cue: You avoided raising a contentious point at dinner.
reply: I said nothing, just to keep the peace.
replyJapanese: 波風を立てないよう、何も言いませんでした。
transferReply: My aunt keeps the peace at every family event.
transferReplyJapanese: 叔母は、家族の集まりのたびに場を丸く収めます。
nuance: Peace takes the. Used for families and groups, and also formally for policing.
nuanceJapanese: peace には the を付ける。家族や集団について使うほか、治安維持の正式な意味もある。

meaning: Stay in contact with someone.
japanese: 連絡を取り合い続ける。
cue: A colleague is leaving the company.
reply: Do keep in touch — I'd like to hear how it goes.
replyJapanese: ぜひ連絡をください。その後の様子を知りたいです。
transferReply: We've kept in touch for twenty years.
transferReplyJapanese: 20年、連絡を取り合っています。
nuance: Touch takes no article. Lose touch is the opposite, and get in touch means making contact.
nuanceJapanese: touch に冠詞は付かない。反対は lose touch、連絡を取ることは get in touch。

meaning: Stop being hard on someone, or give them a chance.
japanese: 大目に見る。あるいは、機会を与える。
cue: A colleague is being criticised for a first mistake.
reply: Give him a break — it's his first month.
replyJapanese: 大目に見てあげてください。まだ初月です。
transferCue: Describe what a talented newcomer needs.
transferReply: All she needs is someone to give her a break.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女に必要なのは、機会をくれる人だけです。
nuance: The person goes between give and a. Informal. A separate lesson teaches give me a break, which expresses disbelief rather than leniency.
nuanceJapanese: 相手は give と a のあいだに置く。くだけた表現。別のレッスンで扱う give me a break は、寛大さではなく不信を表す。

meaning: In a poor state, physically or otherwise.
japanese: 状態がかなり悪い。
cue: Describe a building that has been neglected.
reply: The roof is in a bad way after the winter.
replyJapanese: 冬を越して、屋根はかなり傷んでいます。
transferReply: He was in a bad way last week but he's better now.
transferReplyJapanese: 先週はかなり悪かったのですが、今はよくなっています。
nuance: British and informal. Used for health and for the condition of things.
nuanceJapanese: くだけたイギリス英語。健康にも、物の状態にも使う。

meaning: Remove the obstacles so something can happen.
japanese: 障害を取り除いて、進めるようにする。
cue: An approval removed the last obstacle.
reply: The permit clears the way for building to start.
replyJapanese: 許可が下り、着工への障害がなくなりました。
transferReply: Her resignation cleared the way for a rethink.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女の辞任で、見直しの道が開けました。
nuance: For introduces what can now happen. Way takes the, and the enabler is the subject.
nuanceJapanese: 可能になることは for で示す。way には the を付け、主語は障害を取り除いたもの。

meaning: An idea or word that everyone now uses.
japanese: 広く共有されて、当たり前になった考えや言葉。
cue: A technical term has entered everyday speech.
reply: That phrase has become common currency.
replyJapanese: その言い回しは、すっかり定着しました。
transferReply: The idea is common currency in the industry now.
transferReplyJapanese: その考えは今、業界では当たり前になっています。
nuance: Uncountable, so no article. It describes acceptance, not correctness.
nuanceJapanese: 不可算なので冠詞は付かない。正しさではなく、広まり方を表す。

meaning: Reach the same position as someone ahead.
japanese: 追いついて、並ぶ。
cue: A competitor has caught up. Report it.
reply: They drew level with us in the third quarter.
replyJapanese: 第3四半期に、先方はこちらに並びました。
transferCue: Describe a comeback in a match.
transferReply: The home side drew level just before half-time.
transferReplyJapanese: ホームチームは前半終了間際に、同点に追いつきました。
nuance: British; with introduces the other side. Draw is irregular: drew, drawn.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、相手は with で示す。draw は不規則変化で drew、drawn。

meaning: Secretly intend to get something for yourself.
japanese: ひそかに、それを手に入れようと狙っている。
cue: Someone is quietly positioning for a role.
reply: I think he has designs on the corner office.
replyJapanese: 彼は角部屋の席を、ひそかに狙っていると思います。
transferReply: They have designs on our biggest client.
transferReplyJapanese: 先方は、こちらの最大顧客を狙っています。
nuance: Designs is always plural. It implies the intention is hidden, so it is mildly disapproving.
nuanceJapanese: designs はつねに複数形。意図を隠していることを含意し、やや否定的。

meaning: Refuse to have anything to do with something.
japanese: 一切関わろうとしない。
cue: Someone rejects a practice on principle.
reply: She'll have no truck with unpaid trials.
replyJapanese: 彼女は無給の試用には、一切関わろうとしません。
transferReply: The firm has no truck with late payment.
transferReplyJapanese: その会社は、支払い遅延を一切認めません。
nuance: British and slightly formal, always in the negative. Truck here means dealings, not a vehicle.
nuanceJapanese: やや改まったイギリス英語で、つねに否定形。ここでの truck は車ではなく「関わり」の意味。

meaning: Show clearly that something is not true.
japanese: それが事実でないと、はっきり示す。
cue: Evidence contradicts a widely held belief.
reply: These figures give the lie to that claim.
replyJapanese: この数字が、その主張の誤りを示しています。
transferReply: Her career gives the lie to the whole idea.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女の経歴が、その考え全体の誤りを示しています。
frame: Something gives the lie to something
nuance: Formal. The evidence is the subject, and lie takes the. It disproves rather than merely doubts.
nuanceJapanese: 改まった表現。主語は証拠のほうで、lie には the を付ける。疑うのではなく、反証する。

meaning: Talk while a group listens admiringly.
japanese: 人を集めて、中心で話し続ける。
cue: One guest dominated a gathering pleasantly.
reply: He held court by the fire all evening.
replyJapanese: 彼は暖炉のそばで、一晩じゅう話の中心にいました。
transferReply: She holds court in the staff room every lunchtime.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は昼どきのたびに、職員室で話の中心にいます。
nuance: Court takes no article. Hold is irregular: held. It can be admiring or mildly mocking.
nuanceJapanese: court に冠詞は付かない。hold は不規則変化で held。感心にも軽い皮肉にもなる。

meaning: Said when you are glad something has gone.
japanese: いなくなって、せいせいした。
cue: An unpopular rule has been abolished.
reply: The form has gone, and good riddance.
replyJapanese: あの書式はなくなりました。せいせいします。
transferCue: Describe throwing out a broken item.
transferReply: Good riddance to that chair.
transferReplyJapanese: あの椅子とはお別れです。せいせいしました。
nuance: An exclamation, often with to. Blunt about people, so it is safer about objects and rules.
nuanceJapanese: 感嘆表現で、to を伴うことが多い。人に向けるときついので、物や規則について使うほうが無難。

meaning: Fashionable at the moment.
japanese: 今、流行している。
cue: A style has returned to popularity.
reply: Wide collars are in vogue again.
replyJapanese: 幅広の襟が、また流行しています。
transferReply: That word was in vogue for about a year.
transferReplyJapanese: その言葉は、1年ほど流行していました。
nuance: Vogue takes no article. Slightly formal; all the rage is the informal equivalent. Cambridge lists it under the headword vogue.
nuanceJapanese: vogue に冠詞は付かない。やや改まった表現で、くだけた言い方は all the rage。Cambridge では見出し語 vogue の中に載っている。

meaning: Say who is responsible for something bad.
japanese: 責任の所在を、そこに置く。
cue: A report assigns responsibility for a failure.
reply: The review lays the blame on the process.
replyJapanese: その検証は、責任を手順にあるとしています。
transferReply: Let's not lay the blame at one person's door.
transferReplyJapanese: 責任を一人に負わせるのは、やめましょう。
nuance: Lay is irregular: laid. On or at someone's door introduces who is blamed.
nuanceJapanese: lay は不規則変化で laid。責任を負わせる相手は on か at someone's door で示す。

meaning: Something enjoyable that breaks a serious mood.
japanese: 重い空気をやわらげる、息抜き。
cue: A long serious meeting needed a lighter moment.
reply: The photographs were welcome light relief.
replyJapanese: あの写真は、ありがたい息抜きになりました。
transferCue: Describe a comic scene in a drama.
transferReply: The gardener provides the light relief.
transferReplyJapanese: 庭師の場面が、息抜きの役割を果たしています。
nuance: British and uncountable, so no article. It implies the surrounding material is serious.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語の不可算表現で、冠詞は付かない。周囲が重い内容であることを含意する。

meaning: Matching or suitable for something else.
japanese: ほかのものと調和している。ふさわしい。
cue: A new sign matches the building's style.
reply: The lettering is in keeping with the façade.
replyJapanese: その書体は、正面の意匠と調和しています。
transferReply: His response was in keeping with everything he'd said.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼の対応は、それまでの発言と一貫していました。
nuance: Slightly formal. Out of keeping with is the opposite.
nuanceJapanese: やや改まった表現。反対は out of keeping with。

meaning: Likely to offend people.
japanese: 品位を欠いて、不快感を与える。
cue: A joke was made about a sensitive subject.
reply: That remark was in poor taste.
replyJapanese: あの発言は、品位を欠いていました。
transferCue: Describe an advertisement that caused complaints.
transferReply: The campaign was withdrawn as being in poor taste.
transferReplyJapanese: その広告は、不適切として取り下げられました。
nuance: Bad and poor are both used. Taste takes no article. It judges the choice, not the person.
nuanceJapanese: bad と poor のどちらも使う。taste に冠詞は付かない。人ではなく、その選択を評価する。

meaning: Agree that neither side owes the other anything.
japanese: 貸し借りなしにしようと決める。
cue: You each paid for something of similar value.
reply: You got the tickets, I got dinner — let's call it even.
replyJapanese: チケットはあなた、夕食は私。これで貸し借りなしにしましょう。
transferCue: Settle a small debt between friends.
transferReply: Keep the change and we'll call it even.
transferReplyJapanese: おつりは取っておいて、それでなしにしましょう。
nuance: Fixed with it. Informal, and usually a friendly way to close a small account.
nuanceJapanese: it を伴う固定表現。くだけた言い方で、小さな貸し借りを気持ちよく終える。

meaning: Come out of hiding and become visible.
japanese: 身を隠すのをやめて、表に出る。
cue: Someone who stayed silent finally spoke publicly.
reply: He broke cover with an interview on Monday.
replyJapanese: 彼は月曜の取材で、ついに表に出ました。
transferCue: Describe an animal in a field.
transferReply: A deer broke cover at the edge of the wood.
transferReplyJapanese: 森の端で、鹿が茂みから姿を現しました。
nuance: Cover takes no article. Break is irregular: broke, broken. Literal for animals, figurative for people.
nuanceJapanese: cover に冠詞は付かない。break は不規則変化で broke、broken。動物には文字どおり、人には比喩的に使う。

meaning: Smile, especially when you have been serious.
japanese: 堅い表情を崩して、少し笑う。
cue: Someone stayed serious through a whole meeting.
reply: He didn't crack a smile the whole time.
replyJapanese: 彼は終始、表情ひとつ崩しませんでした。
transferCue: Describe a joke that finally worked.
transferReply: Even she cracked a smile at that one.
transferReplyJapanese: あれには、彼女さえ思わず笑みをこぼしました。
nuance: Informal, and often in the negative. It implies the person was holding a straight face.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、否定形で使うことが多い。それまで真顔を保っていたことを含意する。

meaning: Start chasing someone who is escaping.
japanese: 逃げる相手を、追いかけ始める。
cue: Describe a dog and a squirrel in a park.
reply: The dog gave chase across the whole field.
replyJapanese: その犬は、原っぱ一面を追いかけていきました。
transferReply: Two riders gave chase but never caught up.
transferReplyJapanese: 2人が追走しましたが、追いつけませんでした。
nuance: Chase takes no article in this phrase. Slightly formal or narrative in tone.
nuanceJapanese: この表現では chase に冠詞を付けない。やや改まった、物語的な響き。

meaning: Being considered as a likely candidate or suspect.
japanese: 有力な候補として、名前が挙がっている。
cue: Someone is being considered for a role.
reply: She's in the frame for the Tokyo post.
replyJapanese: 彼女は、東京の職の候補に挙がっています。
transferReply: Three suppliers are still in the frame.
transferReplyJapanese: 3社が、まだ候補に残っています。
frame: Be in the frame for something
nuance: British. For introduces the role. It can also mean being suspected, which context separates.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、役職は for で示す。「容疑者として挙がる」の意味にもなり、文脈で区別する。

meaning: A brief and usually unpleasant encounter with something.
japanese: 一度きりの、ひやりとした関わり。
cue: Someone narrowly avoided a serious problem.
reply: That was his only brush with the law.
replyJapanese: 彼が法に触れかけたのは、あの一度だけです。
transferReply: After a brush with pneumonia, he stopped smoking.
transferReplyJapanese: 肺炎で危ない目にあって、彼は禁煙しました。
nuance: Countable: a brush with. Usually with the law, illness or danger, and always brief.
nuanceJapanese: 可算で a brush with の形。law、illness、danger などと組み合わせ、つねに一時的なもの。

meaning: Go to the door when someone knocks or rings.
japanese: 来客に応じて、玄関に出る。
cue: You are busy and someone is at the door.
reply: Could you answer the door? My hands are wet.
replyJapanese: 玄関に出てもらえますか。手が濡れていて。
transferReply: Nobody answered the door, so I left a note.
transferReplyJapanese: 誰も出なかったので、置き手紙をしました。
nuance: Door takes the. Answer the phone works the same way; neither takes a preposition.
nuanceJapanese: door には the を付ける。answer the phone も同じ形で、どちらも前置詞を取らない。

meaning: In complete harmony with something.
japanese: 完全に調和して、一体になっている。
cue: Describe someone completely comfortable in nature.
reply: He seems at one with the landscape up there.
replyJapanese: あの高地で、彼は風景と一体のようです。
transferCue: Describe a musician and an instrument.
transferReply: She plays as though at one with the cello.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はチェロと一体になったように弾きます。
nuance: Formal and slightly poetic. One takes no article, and with introduces what you are in harmony with.
nuanceJapanese: 改まった、やや詩的な表現。one に冠詞は付かず、調和する対象は with で示す。

meaning: When it suits you, with no hurry.
japanese: 都合のよいときに、急がずに。
cue: You are sending something that needs no fast reply.
reply: Have a look at your leisure and let me know.
replyJapanese: お時間のあるときにご覧いただき、お知らせください。
transferReply: Bring it back at your leisure.
transferReplyJapanese: ご都合のよいときに、お返しください。
nuance: The possessive follows the person. Polite and slightly formal, and it removes any time pressure.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格はその人に合わせる。丁寧でやや改まった表現で、時間の圧力を取り除く。

meaning: Leave quickly to avoid a difficult situation.
japanese: まずいと見て、さっと退散する。
cue: You realised you had walked into an argument.
reply: I beat a retreat before anyone noticed me.
replyJapanese: 気づかれる前に、さっと退散しました。
transferReply: We beat a retreat when the queue doubled.
transferReplyJapanese: 列が倍になったところで、私たちは退散しました。
nuance: Beat is irregular: beat, beaten. Often with hasty. It implies sensible withdrawal, not cowardice.
nuanceJapanese: beat は不規則変化で beat、beaten。hasty を伴うことも多い。臆病ではなく、賢明な撤退を指す。

meaning: Used to add something not connected to the main topic.
japanese: ところで。ついでに言うと。
cue: You remember something unrelated mid-conversation.
reply: By the way, your parcel arrived this morning.
replyJapanese: ところで、今朝あなたの荷物が届きました。
transferCue: Add a detail at the end of a message.
transferReply: By the way, the meeting has moved to three.
transferReplyJapanese: ちなみに、会議は3時に変更になりました。
nuance: Usually opens a sentence, followed by a comma. It marks the point as a side note.
nuanceJapanese: 文頭に置いてコンマを続けるのがふつう。本題から外れた補足であることを示す。

meaning: Despite what has just been said.
japanese: そうは言っても。それでも。
cue: You accept a point but still disagree.
reply: It's cheaper, but even so I'd choose the other.
replyJapanese: 安いのは確かですが、それでも別のほうを選びます。
transferCue: Concede a fact and keep your view.
transferReply: He apologised. Even so, the damage is done.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は謝罪しました。それでも、損害は残ります。
nuance: Opens a clause after a comma or full stop. It concedes a point without changing your conclusion.
nuanceJapanese: コンマやピリオドのあと、節の先頭に置く。指摘は認めつつ、結論は変えない。

meaning: Occasionally, from time to time.
japanese: ときどき。たまに。
cue: Describe how often you visit a place.
reply: We go there every now and again.
replyJapanese: たまに、あそこへ行きます。
transferReply: It fails every now and again for no reason.
transferReplyJapanese: ときどき、理由もなく止まります。
nuance: Again and then are interchangeable. It suggests less often than regularly.
nuanceJapanese: again と then は入れ替えられる。regularly より頻度が低いことを示す。
